name: rearchitect
description: Turn a described architectural problem into up to three applicable design patterns, each with an interface sketch of the refactor it would produce.

interface.shortDescription: Architectural problem → up to 3 design-pattern options with interface sketches.
interface.longDescription: Describe code that is painful to change, extend, test, or reason about. Rearchitect diagnoses the smell against SOLID and a smell catalog, names only the Gang-of-Four patterns whose triggers genuinely fire (up to three), sketches what each refactor's boundary would look like in your language, and recommends one — with 'leave it as it is' always on the table. It proposes options to accept or reject; it does not implement the refactor, audit a whole codebase, or force a pattern where none fits.
defaultPrompt: This class keeps growing and every feature touches it — how should I restructure it?
Every new type means editing the same switch in five files. What pattern fits?
I keep copy-pasting this call sequence everywhere — is there a cleaner structure?
